fields.label: User
fields.description: Owner of the paired device. The token authenticates AS this user.

fields.label: Device
fields.description: Human-readable name the phone reported at pairing (e.g. "Pixel 8"). Client-supplied, so display-only - never trusted for any decision.

fields.label: Platform
fields.description: Client-reported platform (ios / android / web / unknown). Display-only.

fields.label: Enabled
fields.description: 0 = revoked. The auth hook refuses a disabled row, so flipping this kills exactly this one device.

fields.label: Last Used
fields.description: Stamped by the auth hook at most once per throttle window (see jarvis/mobile/device_auth.py), so it is approximate by design - one write per request would be unacceptable on the hot path.

fields.label: Token ID
fields.description: Public half of the device token (`jmd:<token_id>:<secret>`). Not a secret: it only identifies the row to look up.

fields.label: Secret Hash
fields.description: HMAC-SHA256 of the secret, keyed by token_id. The plaintext secret is returned exactly once, at pairing, and NEVER stored - a database dump yields no usable credential.

fields.label: Revoked By
fields.description: Session user at revocation time - a Data SNAPSHOT, not a Link, so the audit trail outlives the account.
